standard_prerequisites.name: The regular-model situation and the degree of an invertible sheaf on a component
standard_prerequisites.statement: The situation fixes a discrete valuation ring with fraction field, residue field and uniformizer, a smooth projective curve over the fraction field, a regular proper model of it, and the irreducible components of the special fibre with their multiplicities; the degree of an invertible sheaf restricted to a component is the degree of the corresponding divisor on the proper curve over the residue field. The author's own situation and the two degree lemmas of the Varieties chapter that the proof quotes are the allowed inputs.
standard_prerequisites.use: The counted lemma builds the pairing that the rest of the section uses to state the symmetry of the intersection numbers of the components, and the statement itself is phrased inside that situation.

core_obligations: Bilinearity in the first argument is immediate from the definition of the pairing as the sum of the coordinates times the degrees of the restrictions; the additivity of the degree under tensor products is the quoted lemma of the Varieties chapter (source line 4714).

For the symmetry it suffices to test on standard basis vectors, so the whole claim reduces to the identity of the two degrees of the restricted invertible sheaves attached to an ordered pair of distinct components (source lines 4715-4721).

For distinct components the canonical section of the sheaf attached to one of them restricts to a nonzero, hence regular, section of its restriction to the other, and its zero scheme is exactly the scheme theoretic intersection of the two components; that intersection is therefore an effective Cartier divisor on the curve, and its degree computes the restricted degree (source lines 4722-4731).
The same computation with the two components interchanged gives the identical expression, which closes the symmetry and hence the lemma (source lines 4732-4734).

proof_roadmap.step: Bilinearity from the definition and the additivity of the degree under tensor products.
Reduce the symmetry to standard basis vectors and therefore to a single identity of two degrees.
Identify the zero scheme of the canonical section with the scheme theoretic intersection and read the degree off that Cartier divisor.
Interchange the two components to obtain the identical expression and conclude.
